# IconButton accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 22    |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 5     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 28    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 9/27  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum).** <!-- 1.4.3:gap:start -->Text inside the button takes the icon color. In `info` (`3.86:1`) and `warning` (`3.11:1`), it is less than `4.5:1` on the default background.<!-- 1.4.3:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.** <!-- 1.4.11:gap:start -->The default focus indicator is the focus ripple, at `1.40:1` to `1.65:1` against white. On the ripple, `info` and `warning` icons are less than `3:1`.<!-- 1.4.11:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.** <!-- 2.2.2:gap:start -->The `loading` spinner turns until `loading` ends, and the user cannot pause it.<!-- 2.2.2:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **2.4.3 Focus Order.** <!-- 2.4.3:gap:start -->A focused button that turns `loading` becomes disabled, and the browser moves focus to the page body.<!-- 2.4.3:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **4.1.3 Status Messages.** <!-- 4.1.3:gap:start -->The `loading` state adds no live region, so a screen reader can miss the change.<!-- 4.1.3:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- The button is one control. While `loading`, it renders a progress indicator before the icon. The icon is `aria-hidden`.
- Order carries meaning only across several controls, such as a toolbar. The surrounding layout sets that order.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In a toolbar or row of icon buttons, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> repeatedly.
2. Write down the order in which the buttons get focus.
3. Compare that order to the visual order.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->focus order matches the visual order. Look for flex layouts that reorder the buttons visually but not in the DOM.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- An icon button has no visible text. Users identify it by its icon, and assistive technology by its accessible name.
- Instructions in the surrounding content must not refer to an icon button by shape, color, or position alone, such as "press the red circle".

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that tells users to operate an icon button.
2. Make sure that it names the action, not only the shape, color, size, or position of the icon.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->each instruction names the action, for example "select Delete", and not only "the trash can on the right".<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.5 Images of Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.4.5:start -->

- The button renders an SVG icon or an icon-font glyph, not text. An icon is not an image of text.
- An image that shows words inside the button is an author choice. Use real text in a `Button` for this.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Inspect each icon button in the product.
2. Make sure that no icon is an image of words, such as a picture of the word "Save".

<!-- 1.4.5:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.5:pass:start -->no icon button shows words as an image. A logo with an accessible name is an exception.<!-- 1.4.5:pass:end -->

#### 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.2.2:start -->

- While `loading`, the button shows a spinning `CircularProgress`. It turns until the application sets `loading` to `false`, and the user cannot pause it. The application can set `loading` without user input.
- If the spinner shows for more than five seconds next to other content, this criterion applies. The essential exception does not apply, because the rest of the page stays interactive.
- On keyboard focus, the focus ripple pulses until focus moves. The user starts it by moving focus.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Set `loading` on an icon button for a task that takes more than five seconds.
2. Look for a way to pause or hide the spinner.

<!-- 2.2.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.2.2:pass:start -->the spinner shows for less than five seconds, or the user can pause or hide it. With the default styles, the user cannot pause it. Keep `loading` short, or show the progress elsewhere.<!-- 2.2.2:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 2.4.11:start -->

- The button is an ordinary focusable element and does not put itself behind other content. Sticky headers, banners, or overlays in the layout can hide it.
- Icon buttons often sit in app bars and toolbars, next to such content.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In a page with a sticky header, footer, or banner, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an icon button near it.
2. Scroll so that the button is under the sticky element.
3. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>.
4. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to move focus back to the button.

<!-- 2.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.11:pass:start -->a part of the focused button stays visible, and the sticky element never fully covers it.<!-- 2.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 3.2.4 Consistent Identification · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 3.2.4:start -->

- The component gives one stable accessible name for each set of props. This is necessary for consistent identification.
- Consistency is a property across pages. Icon buttons have no visible text, so the same icon must have the same function and the same `aria-label` everywhere.

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the icon buttons that do the same job across the product, for example every "Delete".
2. Compare their icons and their `aria-label` values.

<!-- 3.2.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.2.4:pass:start -->the same job uses the same icon and label, and no icon is used for different jobs.<!-- 3.2.4:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.3 Status Messages · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 4.1.3:start -->

- The `loading` state renders a `CircularProgress` with `role="progressbar"`, named after the button. The component adds no `aria-live` or `role="status"` region, so a screen reader can miss the change.
- A focused button that turns `loading` also loses focus, see 2.4.3.
- This applies only when `loading` shows a background task. If the result must be announced, add a live region in the application.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Activate an icon button that goes into the `loading` state for a background task.
3. Listen for an announcement of the loading change.

<!-- 4.1.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.3:pass:start -->the screen reader announces the change without a focus move. It does not, because the component adds no live region. Put the status in a `role="status"` region to fix it.<!-- 4.1.3:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.1.1 Non-text Content · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js` · axe-core `aria-progressbar-name` ✅

<!-- 1.1.1:start -->

- An icon button has no visible text. Its accessible name comes from `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, a `Tooltip` title, or `titleAccess` on the icon. The author must supply it, and the component does not warn when it is missing.
- `SvgIcon` and `Icon` children are `aria-hidden`, unless `SvgIcon` sets `titleAccess`. The author must hide an icon of another type.
- A unit test confirms that `aria-label` names the button and that the icon is hidden. axe-core `button-name` and `aria-command-name`, listed under 4.1.2, confirm that each demo has a name.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each icon button.
3. Listen to the announcement for each button.

<!-- 1.1.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.1.1:pass:start -->each icon button announces its action from its label, for example "Delete file, button", and the icon itself is silent.<!-- 1.1.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- The component sets the correct role: `button`, `link` with `href`, or `role="button"` for a non-native element. It sets the disabled state. While `loading`, the button is disabled and contains a progressbar. axe-core ARIA rules pass on the demos.
- A toggle icon button, such as "Add to favorites", needs `aria-pressed` from the author. axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` confirms that the attribute is valid.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Move the screen-reader cursor to a plain icon button, an `href` icon button, a disabled one, and one with `aria-pressed`. In NVDA, use the arrow keys. In VoiceOver, use <kbd>VO</kbd>+<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd>.
3. Listen to the role and state for each.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the screen reader announces "button", "link", the disabled state, and the pressed state where they apply.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- The purpose of an icon button comes from its icon shape and its label. Focus, disabled, and loading do not rely on color alone.
- The `color` prop only tints the icon. If two buttons differ only by color, for example `error` and `success` with the same icon, the meaning is lost without color.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In a UI with icon buttons of different colors, set the view to grayscale. In Chrome DevTools, open the Rendering tab, then select Emulate vision deficiencies > Achromatopsia.
2. Make sure that you can identify the purpose of each button.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->the purpose of each icon button stays clear without color.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js` · axe-core `color-contrast` ✅

<!-- 1.4.3:start -->

- The documented content is an icon, which 1.4.11 covers. A `Badge` inside the button sets its own colors.
- Text inside the button takes the icon color: `main` for each palette color. A unit test confirms that only `info` and `warning` are less than `4.5:1` on `background.paper`, from the [palette contrast contract](../../test/contrastContract.ts). This is the same as for a `text` Button.
- axe-core `color-contrast` passes on the IconButton demos, which have no colored text.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find icon buttons that render text, for example a letter or a number.
2. With a contrast checker, measure the text against the background behind the button.

<!-- 1.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.3:pass:start -->the text is at least `4.5:1`. `info` and `warning` are the known failures.<!-- 1.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`

<!-- 1.4.11:start -->

- The icon is a graphical object, so it needs `3:1` against the background. A unit test confirms that the icon reaches `3:1` against `background.paper` in the light theme, for `default` and each palette color. `warning` is the lowest, at `3.11:1`.
- On hover, the background gets a `4%` tint of the icon color. A `warning` icon then drops to about `2.98:1`.
- The focus indicator is the focus ripple: the icon color at `30%` opacity. Against white, it is `1.40:1` (`warning`) to `1.65:1` (`secondary`), which is less than `3:1`. `disableRipple` and `disableFocusRipple` remove it.
- The ripple also sits behind the icon. On it, `info` (`2.64:1`) and `warning` (`2.22:1`) icons are less than `3:1`.
- The `loading` spinner uses `action.disabled`, about `1.88:1` against white. The button is disabled while it shows, so the exemption for inactive components can apply. This needs a review.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure each icon against the background behind the button. Do this for each `color` in use.
2. Hover over a `warning` icon button and measure the icon against the hover background.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an icon button so that the focus ripple shows.
4. Measure the focus ripple against the adjacent colors, and the icon against the ripple.

<!-- 1.4.11:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.11:pass:start -->each icon and the focus indicator are at least `3:1`. Disabled buttons are exempt. The default focus ripple fails. Enable the `focusVisible` theme ring to fix it.<!-- 1.4.11:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.3 Focus Order · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`

<!-- 2.4.3:start -->

- The button is one tab stop in DOM order, with no positive `tabIndex`. A disabled or loading button leaves the tab order. Unit tests confirm this.
- A focused button that turns `loading` becomes disabled. Chromium then moves focus to the page body, so the next <kbd>Tab</kbd> starts again from the top of the page. The unit tests run in jsdom too, which keeps focus on the button, so they do not show this.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an icon button that turns `loading` when you activate it.
2. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> again, and note which element gets focus.

<!-- 2.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.3:pass:start -->focus moves to the next element after the button. It moves to the top of the page, because the button loses focus. Move focus to a nearby element before you set `loading`.<!-- 2.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `link-name` ✅

<!-- 2.4.4:start -->

- This applies only with `href`, where the root is an `<a>`. axe-core `link-name` confirms that the link in the fixture has a name.
- An icon link has no visible text, so the `aria-label` alone must tell the destination.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find icon buttons that use `href`.
2. Read the `aria-label` of each, together with the content around it.

<!-- 2.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.4:pass:start -->a user can tell where each link goes, for example "Open settings" and not "Link".<!-- 2.4.4:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The accessible name is the label of the control. axe-core `button-name` and `link-name` confirm that it is present.
- Whether the label describes the action is an authoring concern. Icon buttons often get vague labels, such as "icon" or "button".

**Manual testing steps**

1. List the `aria-label` of each icon button.
2. Read each label without its icon.

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->each label tells the action, for example "Delete file", not "delete icon".<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.7 Focus Visible · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 2.4.7:start -->

- Keyboard focus shows the focus ripple. A mouse click does not show it. A Playwright test confirms that keyboard focus changes how the button looks.
- `disableRipple` and `disableFocusRipple` remove the ripple. Then the button has no focus indicator.
- With `focusVisible: true` on the theme, keyboard focus draws an outline ring that does not use the ripple (see [Focus visible](https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/focus-visible/)). A Playwright test confirms the ring with the ripple disabled.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an icon button. Make sure that a focus indicator shows, and that it looks different from the hover style.
2. Click an icon button with the mouse. Make sure that the focus indicator does not show.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to an icon button with `disableRipple` and the default theme. Make sure that no indicator shows, which the author must fix.
4. Set `focusVisible: true` on the theme. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the same button. Make sure that the outline ring shows.

<!-- 2.4.7:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.7:pass:start -->each icon button shows a visible indicator on keyboard focus. With `disableRipple`, the indicator comes from the `focusVisible` theme ring or from author styles.<!-- 2.4.7:pass:end -->

#### 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) · AA

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: axe-core `target-size` ✅

<!-- 2.5.8:start -->

- The size depends on the icon. With an icon that inherits the button font size, `small` is 28 px (an 18 px icon and 5 px padding), `medium` is 40 px, and `large` is 52 px.
- The default `SvgIcon` size makes `small` 34 px. A child smaller than 14 px makes `small` smaller than 24 px.
- axe-core `target-size` confirms the size on the demos and fixtures. A fixture has a row of `small` buttons with no gap. `edge` adds a negative margin on one side, which can put the button against other targets.

**Manual testing steps**

1. In browser DevTools, select an icon button with `size="small"`.
2. Read the width and height of its box.

<!-- 2.5.8:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.5.8:pass:start -->the width and height are at least 24 CSS px, or a 24 px circle on the target does not touch another target.<!-- 2.5.8:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-command-name` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `button-name` ✅, `duplicate-id-aria` ✅, `link-name` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- A native `<button>`, an `<a>` with `href`, and `role="button"` on a non-native element each set the correct role. `disabled` and `loading` disable the button, and the loading progressbar takes its name from the button. Unit tests and the axe-core `aria-*` rules, `button-name`, and `nested-interactive` confirm this.
- ARIA makes the children of a `button` presentational. Some screen readers do not announce the progressbar inside it. A screen-reader review must confirm this.
- The author supplies the name with `aria-label` and the pressed state with `aria-pressed`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a native icon button, an `href` icon button, and a non-native one.
3. Disabled and loading buttons are not in the tab order. Move the screen-reader cursor to them. In NVDA, use the arrow keys. In VoiceOver, use <kbd>VO</kbd>+<kbd>Right Arrow</kbd>.
4. Listen to the name, role, and state for each.
5. Set `loading` and listen for the change to the disabled state.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->the name, role, and state are correct for each kind, and the disabled one announces "disabled" and the `href` one "link".<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.4 Resize Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.4:start -->

- The icon size uses `rem`, so the icon scales with the text size. A `Badge` count inside the button is the only documented text.
- A Playwright test confirms that the badge demo does not clip or overflow at a 200% text size.

<!-- 1.4.4:end -->

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- The button size comes from its padding and its icon, from 28 to 52 CSS px. It does not cause horizontal scrolling at 320 px, which a Playwright test confirms. A toolbar that does not wrap is a layout concern.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

#### 1.4.12 Text Spacing · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.12:start -->

- The button sets no fixed height or `overflow`, so text inside it, such as a `Badge` count, is not clipped. A Playwright test applies the WCAG text-spacing values to the badge demo.

<!-- 1.4.12:end -->

#### 2.1.1 Keyboard · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`, `ButtonBase.test.js`

<!-- 2.1.1:start -->

- A native `<button>` activates with <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd>. A unit test confirms this. The [`ButtonBase` tests](../ButtonBase/ButtonBase.test.js) cover the non-native case.

<!-- 2.1.1:end -->

#### 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`

<!-- 2.1.2:start -->

- The button is one focusable control and does not capture focus. A unit test confirms that <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> move focus in and out.

<!-- 2.1.2:end -->

#### 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`

<!-- 2.5.2:start -->

- Activation runs on `click`, on the pointer up-event. A unit test confirms that a release off the button cancels the activation.

<!-- 2.5.2:end -->

#### 2.5.3 Label in Name · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `label-content-name-mismatch` ✅

<!-- 2.5.3:start -->

- An icon-only button has no visible text, so there is nothing to match.
- Visible text inside the button, such as a `Badge` count, must be part of the name. axe-core `label-content-name-mismatch` confirms this on the badge demo.
- A `Tooltip` gives its title as the name. If you also set `aria-label`, it replaces the title, so keep the two the same.

<!-- 2.5.3:end -->

#### 3.2.1 On Focus · A

`✅ Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`

<!-- 3.2.1:start -->

- Focus shows only the focus ripple. A unit test confirms that focus does not activate the button.

<!-- 3.2.1:end -->

#### 3.2.2 On Input · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `IconButton.test.js`

<!-- 3.2.2:start -->

- A change to `aria-pressed` does not move focus and does not run `onClick`. A unit test confirms this. Only a real activation runs the handler. A change to `loading` moves focus, see 2.4.3.

<!-- 3.2.2:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A).** <!-- 3.3.2:start -->A plain icon button asks for no input. The Button report rates the file-upload pattern (`component="label"` with a hidden input).<!-- 3.3.2:end -->
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), 44 px.** `small` and `medium` are smaller than 44 px. Only `large` (52 px) is larger. `🚩`
- **2.4.13 Focus Appearance.** The focus ripple does not meet it, because its contrast is `1.40:1` to `1.65:1`. `🚩`
- **2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.** The ripple honors `prefers-reduced-motion` when the theme sets `motion.reducedMotion`. The default is `never`. `disableRipple` also removes it. `🚩`

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The IconButton component in isolation, rendered through its documented API.
- **Automated.** axe-core in the Playwright test harness, on the IconButton demos and fixtures in [`buttons.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/buttons/buttons.a11y.json). Interaction tests are in `IconButton.test.js` and `ButtonBase.test.js`.
- **Assistive-technology review.** Not done yet. The flagged criteria come from a review of the source. A review with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver must still confirm them.

<!-- scope:end -->
